text:
marta: Heads-up — saw steady memory accounting drift when continuous-batching grows past ~80 active sequences. pad% jumps and we hit workspace OOMs intermittently. reproducer attached :eyes:

marta: quick numbers from yesterday's run: batch_count=1200, avg_batch_size=72 -> 98, pad_bytes went from ~1.8GB to ~5.4GB (12% -> 36%), kv_cache retained ~3.2GB, workspace_watermark=9.6GB, free_slab=400MB

raj: can you paste the profiler trace? curious if kernel selection flips at that seq distribution boundary and causes extra temp allocation.

marta: pasted a trimmed trace (dev-run):
```
[profiler] step=812 trace:
  batch.size=96 seq_len.p50=512 p90=1536 p99=1984
  kernel=attn_fused_v2 -> fallback to attn_split at seq >= 1536
  alloc: pad_buffer 5.4GB workspace_req 10.1GB kv_cache_committed 3.2GB
  allocator: slab_pool(16GB) used=13.6GB fragments=1.1GB
  OOM: workspace_alloc failed @ 10.1GB required
```

li: hm, that kernel switch at 1536 makes sense. attn_split creates additional temporary buffers per head, which increases peak workspace beyond what our pad accounting assumes. continuous batch growth means multiple sequences cross that threshold in the same batch -> amplification.

frank: two levers here: 1) tighten kernel selection boundary or prefer a quantized variant that has smaller scratch, 2) make allocator reserve a per-kernel extra headroom when mixture of kernels present. both need experiments.

marta: also saw per-seq overhead creeping up: small sequences still carry a ~5KB metadata + 24B per-token tagging in the workspace (we forgot to strip some debug headers in the pooling path).

raj: can we reproduce with a small local run? command I used to stress this: 
```
python -m rdinfer.bench --model gpt-medium --batcher continuous --target_throughput 1200 --max_seq 2048 --seed 42
```
should flip kernels predictable.

bench-bot: quick run with two configs:
- baseline (allocator=frugal-v1, kernel-crossover=1536): pad% avg=34.7 p99_latency=162ms p50=48ms OOMs=3/10 runs
- experiment (allocator=frugal-v2+reuse_pool, kernel-crossover=1792): pad% avg=18.2 p99_latency=175ms p50=50ms OOMs=0/10 runs
(note: throughput regressed ~4% in experiment but stable)

li: interesting — reuse_pool helps a lot. probably reduces fragmentation and amortizes per-batch temp allocations. p99 latency increase is small compared to avoiding OOMs.

marta: can we try a hybrid: adaptive kernel routing + per-gpu "scratch-reserve" slab of 512MB for attn_split peaks? gives margin without pushing global allocator policies.

frank: also consider per-seq bucketing: group sequences into buckets by length and do intra-bucket continuous batches rather than mixing wide seq ranges. reduces padding massively. downside: scheduling complexity + slight latency jitter for small seqs.

raj: quick prototype patch: allocator: add flag `reuse_last_buffer=true` and `scratch_reserve_mb=512`. put in sandbox for perf run.

dev-bot: CI job queued: https://ci.redwood/infra/12345 — bench matrix includes frugal-v2 and kernel-crossover variants.

marta: on KV cache side: we should evict tail entries more aggressively when a batch spikes workspace. observed KV retention prevented reclaiming ~2.4GB that could've saved us. code path: `kv_cache.commit_on_finalize=false` in continuous mode — maybe flip to true under high-watermark.

li: or implement immediate soft-eviction: if workspace pressure > 85% then evict oldest segments until below 70%. cheap to implement as heuristic.

bench-bot: soft-evict test results:
- soft-evict at 85%: pad% avg=20.1 p99_latency=168ms OOMs=0
- hard-evict at 70%: pad% avg=17.0 p99_latency=180ms OOMs=0 (higher latency due to extra KV fetches)

marta: notes from memory accounting audit: our pad estimation ignores per-request metadata + token-attrs arrays (~8-12KB per seq) which at large batch counts adds up. opened issue to zero debug headers and compress token meta arrays for continuous path.

frank: action items:
- marta: run A/B with `allocator=frugal-v2+reuse_pool` + `scratch_reserve_mb=512` (3 runs, mixed seed) — collect pad% + p99 latency + OOM count by route
- li: prototype soft-evict heuristic in kv layer and add metric `kv_evictions_soft` to console
- raj: try adaptive kernel crossover policy based on observed seq distribution in batch (if >25% sequences >= crossover, prefer split variant)

marta: I'll land the debug-strip patch too (reduces per-seq overhead ~6KB).

li: once we have metrics, let's create a quick dashboard slice: per-route pad%, kv_evictions, workspace_watermark, kernel_variant_ratio. makes regression detection obvious.

raj: FYI I pushed a tiny profiler helper to `tools/batch_profiler` that annotates kernel switches per batch. bench-bot will pick it up.
